articles.title: Indian Rupee Makes Strong Comeback Against Dollar! How Trump, FIIs & RBI Changed The Game
articles.description: The Indian Rupee is staging a remarkable comeback against the US Dollar, strengthening from ₹95.26 on October 29 to around ₹93.85 on November 9. But what triggered this sudden turnaround? The recovery follows a major political shift in the United States, easing tensions with Iran, falling crude oil prices and renewed foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows into Indian stock markets. After months of intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), global developments are finally providing relief to the Indian currency. With HSBC, Goldman Sachs and Citi turning increasingly bullish on Indian equities, could the rupee strengthen further? What does a stronger rupee mean for petrol prices, inflation, gold, silver, foreign travel, overseas education and Indian companies? And could upcoming US inflation data and Federal Reserve decisions reverse the rally? Watch Business Today TV's special report on the rupee recovery, its impact on your money and what happens next.

articles.title: German Giants Cut Jobs at Home: Can India Take Germany's Engineering Crown? | The Great Reversal
articles.description: Germany built its economic might on engineering excellence. Today, its industrial heartland is battling job cuts, factory closures and intensifying competition. Schaeffler alone plans to cut over 3,000 jobs across Europe, including 2,660 in Germany. At the same time, India is moving beyond being a market for German companies. It is becoming a destination for engineering, research, innovation and global product development. Mercedes-Benz chairman Ola Källenius says there is “India in every single Mercedes.” As Germany struggles to sustain its industrial edge, India is becoming an increasingly indispensable part of its engineering future. But does doing the work also mean owning the technology? On Beyond Borders, Ananya Dasgupta explores the changing equation between Germany's industrial legacy and India's growing global engineering role.
